title: Revolt of 1857
intro: Lapse. Dalhousie by Doctrine of lapse, annexed Jhansi to British Empire in 1854. *In June, 1857, the revolt began in Jhansi under the leadership of Rani Laxmi Bai (the revolt in Jhansi was outbreaked/began by sepoys Laxmibai Later assumed control and led resistance). She died on 17/18 June, 1858 A.D. ﬁ ghting General Hugh Henry Rose . On her death, Hugh Rose said, “Among the Indian revolutionaries the women lying here is the only man.” *Revolt in Lucknow began under the leadership of Begum Hazrat Mahal on 30 th May, 1857 A.D. She declared her minor son Birjis Qadr as Nawab and took to all affairs of the Lucknow into herself. On 21 st March, 1858 A.D., Campbell with the help of Gurkha Regiment regained Lucknow. *On 5 June 1857, the rebel repoys halted at Kalyanpur; on 6 June they returned to Kanpur, where Nana Saheb (Nana Dhondhu Pant) assumed their leadership. He was later proclaimed/declared Peshwa at Kanpur (on June 30, 1857 as recorded by R.C. Majumdar) and the war of Independence spread in Kanpur. He was helped a lot by Commander-in-Chief (his General Military Advisor) Tatya Tope, The original name of Tatya Tope was Ramchandra Pandurang Tope . After being betrayed by a close friend Man Singh, he was captured when he was camping in a forest. Tope was captured on 7 April 1859, after a hurried trial the military court gave the verdict on 15th April 1859 punishing him with death by hanging and he was hanged on 18th April 1859 at Sipri/Shivpuri. *Kunwar Singh led the revolt from Jagdishpur (currently Bhojpur district), Bihar. He was from Shahabad region of Bihar. *Maniram Dutt Deewan in Assam declared Kandarpeswar Singha, the grandson of the last king as the king and planned an armed insurrection conspiracy. But soon after Maniram Deewan was caught and hanged for his promotional activities regarding the revolt. *Thakur Kushal Singh of Auwa defeated the combined army of English and Jodhpur. *Maulavi Ahmadullah Shah provided leadership to the revolt from Faizabad (Ayodhya) in 1857 A.D. He was a determined opponent of British rule. He was native to Chinapattan of Madras, but he migrated to Faizabad. He asked all the different religious believers to stand as one against these English foreigners and to wipe them out from India. About him, Britishers said a man of great abilities, of undaunted courage of stern determination; and best soldier among the rebels. A bounty of Rs. 50,000 was placed on his arrest (dead or alive). *Mirza Ghalib saw the revolt of 1857 A.D. with his own eyes. He was born on 27 th December, 1797 AD in Agra and died in Delhi on 15 th February, 1869. *Shindhiyas of Gwalior helped the Britishers in the suppression of the Revolt.* Minister of Gwalior Sir Dinkar Rao was praised by European historians for his loyalty to English. Minister of Hyderabad Salar Jung was praised in the same way for his loyalty. *The revolt of 1857 was spread over a wide area and was substantially supported by the public. But still, this Revolt was unable to bring whole of India together. This revolt did not become an all-India revolt; South India remained largely quiet, while Bengal and Punjab were only marginally affected though parts of eastern and western India were involved. *Scindia of Gwalior, Holkar of Indore, Nizam of Hyderabad, King of Jodhpur, Nawab of Bhopal, Sikh rulers of Patiala, Nabha and Jind and other Sikh Sardar of Punjab, Maharaja of Kashmir and other kings were actively helping the Britishers in suppressing the revolts. To these rulers, Governor-General Canning said, that these rulers acted as barriers against the high and fast-moving wave of seas, in the absence of which we would have washed out from India completely. The Educated Class didn’t show any interest in the Revolt of 1857 they generally remained neutral or sided with the British, viewing the rebellion as a regressive, reactionary and anti-modern movement; which was one of the major causes of the failure of this Revolt. *Lord Canning (1856-62 A.D.) was the Governor-General during the revolt of 1857. During the Revolt, he made Allahabad as an emergency headquarter. Lord Canning was the last Governor-General appointed by the Company and was the ﬁ rst Viceroy appointed by the British Crown. *Under the judicial reforms, Indian High Court Act, 1861 established High Courts at Bombay, Calcutta and Madras. After enabling 1861 Act, the courts were formally established by the ‘Letters Patent of 1862 under Lord Canning. Under the social reforms Canning passed Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 . The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 is known as First War of Independence in India and as an Indian Mutiny in England. *Sir Syed Ahmed Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind which was written/ submitted in 1858 and published in 1859 A.D.* R.C Majumdar was appointed by Government of India to write on the Revolt of 1857, but due to differences with the government committee he rejected this proposal, and he published his book “The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857” on his own in 1957 (although his original proposal was turned down in ﬁ rst instance, later he became member of ‘Board of Editors’ for history of the freedom movement but later discontinued with this service & wrote independently). *R.C. Majumdar said, “ It is difﬁ cult to avoid the conclusion that the so-called First National War of Independence of 1857 is neither First, nor National, nor a war of Independence”. *Most important outcome of 1857 was the Queen’s Proclamation of 1858. It was declared on 1 st November, 1858 in Allahabad by Lord Canning ending the Company Rule and putting the Realm of British India under the direct control of Crown. This declaration included no extension of British India’s then present territorial possessions no further interference in the religious matters of people, equal protection of law to be available to all. British stopped all further annexation of native states and kings were allowed to adopt. *Approximately after the Suppression of 1857 Revolt, ‘ Peel Commission ’ was constituted for the reorganization of Indian Army by British Government. The Commission divided the army on the basis of caste, religion, race, community, etc. The number of European Indian History General Studies B–399 soldiers was increased from 45,000 in 1857 A.D. to 65,000 by 1863 A.D. Indian troops were reduced from 2,38,000 to 1,40,000.The ratio of Europeans to Indian soldiers in Bengal was 1:2 whereas in Madras and Bombay it was 1:3. After the Revolt the soldiers the recruitment of Gorkha, Sikh and Punjab is increased * John Bennet Hearsey was the commanding ofﬁ cer of Barrakpore when Revolt of 1857 broke out there. *Viscount Palmerston was the then Prime Minister of United Kingdom. His tenure as Prime Minister was from 1855 to 1858 and 1859 to 1865. *The Revolt was poorly organized with least coordination or nominal central leadership. The rebels lacked a clear understanding of Colonial Rule, they have a myopic views of forward-looking programme, a coherent ideology, a political perspective or societal alternatives. Although of ﬁ cial sources record substantial Hindu-Muslim and inter-regional unity among many rebels, but many central leaderships lack unity and which proved to be detrimental to this revolt. Modern Nationalism was not known to them at that time, which led to everyone ﬁ ghting for their own interests and not for the nation. Except with the common shared hatred for alien rule in their own land. *Brigadier General John Nicholson died on 23 rd September, 1857, Who was wounded nine days before while leading his men to capture Delhi. The Delhi was captured by British on September 20-21, 1857. Sir Henry Montgomery Lawrence Chief Commissioner of Oudh (‘Lawrence of Lucknow’), mortally wounded on July 2, died on July 4, 1857 in Lucknow in the 1857 revolt while protecting British residency. Brigadier- General James George Smith Neill died in September 1857 while attempting to reach the Residency during the siege. Major-General Sir Henry Havelock was died on dysentery in November 1857 a few days after the siege was lifted. Sir James Outram and W. Taylor termed the Revolt of 1857 as a result of a conspiracy of Hindu and Muslim. Outram said that this was a Muslim conspiracy in which the Hindus concerns were used for the Revolt. It was only a Sepoy Mutiny, according to John Lawrence and Seeley. According to T.R. Holmes, it was a war between Barbarism and Civilization. V . D. Savarkar in his book “The Indian War of Independence 1857”, termed this Revolt as an organized struggle for Independence. He said it was the First War of Independence. * Surendra Nath Sen whose book ‘Eighteen Fifty-Seven’ was published in 1957 was commissioned by Indian government to write history of 1857 and was the ﬁ rst Director of the National Archives of India.

title: Other Civil Uprisings
intro: The Crown was empowered to appoint a Governor-General and the Governors of the Presidencies. An Indian Civil Service was to be created under the control of the secretary of state. All the property and other assets of the East India Company were transferred to the crown. The crown also assumed the responsibilities of the company along with their related treaties, contracts and so forth.

title: Development of Education in Modern India
intro: Society was established and Vishnushastri Chiplunkar, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Mahadeo Ballal Namjoshi, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar and Vaman Shivram Apte were the main founders of the Society. *Raja Ram Mohan Roy was among the earliest propagators of Modern Education in India. He along with David Hare established famous “ Hindu College ” in 1817 A.D. *Mayo College was established in Ajmer in 1875 A.D. Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was established in Aligarh in 1875 A.D. Delhi College was established in 1824 A.D.* Madan Mohan Malaviya advocated religious teachings in the Indian Universities. *In 1916, he established Banaras Hindu University and was the vice-chancellor of BHU from 1919 to 1939 A.D.. He published several magazines and Newspapers in English and Hindi such as Hindustan, India Union, Abhyudaya, Maryada, etc.

title: Development of Press in Modern India
intro: Indian History General Studies B–435 Development of Press in Modern India *James Augustus Hicky in 1780 A.D. started the Bengal Gazette, the ﬁ rst newspaper in India. Lord Wellesley enacted Censorship of Press Regulations, 1799 . It imposed almost wartime press restrictions including pre-censorship. In 1807 this Act included pamphlets, books and magazines too. *Lord Hastings in 1818 abolished the strict pre-censorship of the press in India and dispensed with their submitting their papers to an ofﬁ cer of government previous to publications. Vernacular Press Act, 1878 was passed during the tenure of Lord Lytton (1876-1880 A.D.). The Act empowered the district magistrate to call upon the printer and publisher of any vernacular newspaper to enter into a bond with the government not to cause disaffection against the government or antipathy between persons of different religion, caste, race, through published material. *The press and publisher could also be required to deposit security which could be forfeited if the regulation were violated, and press equipment could be seized if the offence reoccurred. *Under this Act, proceedings were instituted against Som Prakash, Bharat Mihir, Dacca Prakash and Samachar. *B. G. Tilak was imprisoned for anti-British journalism in 1882. He was the ﬁ rst Indian to be punished for the performance of his duty in this ﬁ eld. *Tilak was arrested after the murder of W.C. Rand and ofﬁ cer Charles Ayerst on the grounds of the publication of a poem, “Shivaji’s utterances” in Kesari, and a speech that Tilak had delivered at the Shivaji festival, justifying Afzal’s Khan murder by Shivaji. Tilak’s defence of Shivaji’s killing of Afzal Khan was portrayed by the prosecution as an incitement to kill British ofﬁ cials. In 1897, he was imprisoned for 18 months for inciting Chapekar brothers for killing W.C. Rand and Charles Ayerst through his articles published in Kesari (he was charged for sedition for writing such articles). * 'The Free Hindustan' newspaper was started by Tarak Nath Das in North America (Vancouver). *Raja Ram Mohan Roy used the press as a medium to express and publish his views. In 1821 he published ‘Sambad Kaumudi’ Bengali weekly newspaper. After one year he published a newspaper ‘Mirat- ul-Akhbar’ in the Persian language. ‘ Indian Mirror’ was published from Calcutta (Bengal). Credit for establishment of Indian Mirror (1861) goes to Debendranath Tagore and Manmohan Ghosh. * Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakana and Kartar Singh Sarabha, etc. founded Hindustan Ghadar Party (Ghadar Party) in USA and Canada to free India from British Rule. ‘Ghadar’ a weekly publication, was a manifesto of the party which was ﬁ rst published on 1st November, 1913 at San Francisco in Urdu. From 9 th December, 1913 A.D. its printing in Gurmukhi script also started. It was later on published in Marathi, Hindi, English and Gujarati. Its one edition was also published in Pashto language. *Amrit Bazar Patrika, a Bengali (later English) weekly was launched February 20, 1868, in the village of Palua Magura in the Jessore district of Present day Bangladesh, through the efforts of Sishir Kumar and Motilal Ghosh. But later it started being published from Kolkata (West Bengal), but to escape the Vernacular Press Act, it got converted to English format overnight in 1878 A.D. *Girish Chandra Ghosh started ‘The Bengalee’ in 1862 A.D. which was transferred to S.N. Banerjee in 1879 A.D. Girish Chandra Ghosh started the Hindoo Patriot. Later on, Harish Chandra Mukherjee became its editor. *In 1881 A.D., Tilak published two newspapers Kesari and Mahratta in Poona (now Pune). Kesari in Marathi was the main newspaper of Tilak’s Home Rule Movement. Earlier Gopal Ganesh Agarkar was the ﬁ rst editor of Kesari. The ﬁ rst editor of the Maratta/ Maratha was Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Mahratta was published in English. *Bangwasi, Kaal, Kesari etc. Newspaper supported the revolutionary movements and criticized the moderate policies of Congress. Sandhya, Yugantar and Kaal, advocated revolutionary extremism during the freedom struggle. *Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar in 1858 started publishing ‘Som Prakash’ newspaper, it supported the interests of the Indigo revolutionaries. Vidyasagar mooted the original idea of the newspaper, it was ﬁ rst edited by Dwarkanath Vidyabhushan. The Free Press Journal is an English-language daily newspaper that was established by Swaminathan Sadanand. * Indian opinion was started by Mahatma Gandhi in 1903 A.D. in South Africa. Mansukh Lal Hiralal Nazar was its ﬁ rst editor. It was published in Gujarati, Hindi, Tamil and English. *Young India was published bi-weekly from Bombay from 7 May 1919 A.D. under supervision of Gandhiji. Jamanadas Dwarakadas and Shankarlal Banker were its foundational member Shankar Lal Banker was its publisher. On 8th October, 1919 A.D. title: Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)
intro: Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) *Clement Attlee became British Prime Minister on 26 th July, 1945 A.D. They arrived on March 24, 1946 A.D. and held extensive discussions in April with almost all major leaders of the country. The Cabinet Mission proposed a three-tier polity for India. The major recommendation of the Cabinet Mission was to divide the provinces into three sections i.e. A, B and C. * On 16 th May, 1946 A.D. Cabinet Mission announced its recommendations and its main proposals were- (1) There should be a Union of India, embracing both British India and the states, which should deal with the following subjects – foreign affairs, defence and communications; of India would be given Independence. (2) The Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan was rejected. (3) The Union should have an Executive and Legislature constituted from British India Province and Princely State Representatives. (4) A Constituent Assembly would be formed with the representatives of Provincial Legislative Assembly Chief Commissioners Provinces and the Princely States. *Cabinet Mission also recommended reorganization of Viceroy’s Executive Council and formation of the interim government in which all the ministerial posts including war member would be held by Indians. *Gandhiji supported Cabinet Mission and said this proposal is the best document the British Government could have produced in the circumstances, while cautioning that their best may possible be harmful.
